json.reasoning: Confirmed real and squarely a SPEC gap (a), not a code defect (b). The spec (staking_pool_specs.move lines 171-179) contains exactly one statement before the call -- asserts(split_amount <= fungible_staked_sui_value(...)) -- and ZERO ensures, so it proves only abort-freedom and verifies nothing about behavior: conservation, result.value == split_amount, result.pool_id preservation, and the value decrement are all unverified. I traced the implementation (staking_pool.move lines 517-530): the assert guards the subtraction against underflow, fungible_staked_sui.value becomes old_value - split_amount, and the returned object gets value = split_amount with the same pool_id and a fresh UID. Conservation holds by construction: (old - split) + split == old. I considered (b) and rejected it -- there is no arithmetic that can drift, no aliasing, and per the writeup the function does not touch StakingPool state or FungibleStakedSuiData.total_supply, so the only mutated state is the two objects' value fields, which sum to the original. Therefore adding the conservation ensures (with the original value captured before the call) would PASS the prover -- tightening the spec would not expose any system bug, the hallmark of an (a) issue. Severity is high because conservation is the function's single headline correctness property and the spec currently asserts nothing about it (or any other effect); a future regression in the split arithmetic -- e.g. copying the wrong value into the result or a wrong subtraction -- would go entirely uncaught. The function is user-facing (called directly, not gated by an entry point), which raises the value of a complete contract. Confidence high: verified directly against both source files.
